name: Pavlina
desc: Grand Duchess of the Snegurochka from the House of Hesperides.

customize.name: Fae
customize.desc: Followers of the first Cryo Archon, the Belyi Tsar, who were created from the bones of giant beasts and fallen frostmoon light.

customize.text: Pavlina is a Snegurochka — a race that lives for love. Snegovik were created inferior, without a soul. They can only obtain a soul through a ritual of marrying a human.

After the Proto-Man was divided into three parts, a third of his power became Ikhor. The princess of the Snegurochka tried to use this fragment to imbue all Snegovik with a soul through a ritual. customize.name: Invitation to the "Ritual"
customize.desc:
A wondrous invitation that always seems to find its way into the hands of its rightful recipient.
With this invitation, one may journey to the House of Hesperides atop the icy peaks of Snezhnaya, to attend the wedding of Pavlina, the princess of the Snegurochka.

customize.name: Severed Fragment of Ikhor
customize.desc:
A fragment of Ikhor's power, split off by Aksinya when the "ritual" was interrupted.
For some reason, it has taken the form of a glowing doll. Perhaps the desire to "fulfill the wishes of others" became the strings that controlled him long ago, and now he is nothing more than a puppet carrying a form of transcendent power.

customize.name: Pebble of Freezing Heart
customize.desc:
An egg-shaped stone infused with the power required for the Eye of Graeae to reclaim his physical form.
Once used by the fae Grand Duchess Pavlina to remedy the inherent flaws of the fae.
Hidden within it may lie the aspiration of how a mere mortal might ascend to a higher status through rebirth.

customize.name: Proto-Man
customize.desc: The Key, created as a result of countless experiments, was supposed to help the Belyi Tsar become the Primordial Human.

customize.name: Eye of Graeae
customize.desc:
A strange mechanism you encountered in an abandoned station. It often appears in the form of a monocle.

It offers many convenient functions, such as recording blueprints for Prime Ice constructs, creating Prime Ice, calling trains.

...Perhaps it was built for the very purpose of providing all these conveniences.

customize.text:
<color=#ffd680>Regarding the Snegurochka and their princess...</color>
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : As for the Snegurochka and the Grand Duchess here... Do you have any questions about them?
<color=#36ffff>Traveler</color> : Tell me about the Snegurochka...
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : "Snegurochka" is not a formal term of address. Rather, it is a common name for a female "Snegovik"... which first appeared — so it would seem — in a romantic novel.
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : However, that romantic novel was well researched and had a firm grasp of the peculiarities of Snegovik at large... "Snegovik live for love."
<color=#36ffff>Traveler</color> : Why do they call them a race that lives for love?
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : Hmm... This is merely one research perspective, rather than fact, and thus may not be true. However, it goes like this:
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : Snegovik were created to seek love. Amongst the many types of fae, they were created for "companionship," and in this, their souls have been lacking since birth.
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : As such, they will seek out human "companionship" and thus gain fulfillment. Following this, a Snegovik who has completed their "companionship" will no longer be bound by this constraint that is engraved into their lives... This is also why Snegovik suddenly turn cruel or devoid of emotion at some point in tales involving them. And in other stories, Snegovik who cannot attain love suffer for it and die — such outcomes are commonplace.
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : That is the type of fae Snegovik are.
<color=#36ffff>Traveler</color> : Tell me about the princess of the Snegurochka...
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : Pavlina, present-day princess of the Snegurochka... She is, if memory serves, also an Hvergelmir member.
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : Her skill at fashioning Prime Ice is unmatched in all Snezhnaya. As such, little can be done regarding any techniques related to this material without her support...
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : However, her reputation amongst her kind is not stellar... Some Snegovik find her emotionally indifferent, and that she does not pursue the "love" that they should. That she is not a proper Snegovik... unlike her then-competitor for the seat of princess, Larisa.
<color=#ffd680>Regarding Pavlina's experiments...</color>
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : It seems that Pavlina once used Hvergelmir's techniques to modify Snegovik...
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : Using the Eitr, she could cause a Snegovik's body to gain power surpassing their race's due.
<color=#36ffff>Traveler</color> : What is the Eitr?
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : The Eitr is a product of forbidden Hyperborean research. The master crafters of the once-glorious golden city had grasped the technology needed to modify the very essence of life. It was... the final result of that forbidden technology...
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : His Majesty the Belyi Tsar appears to have obtained it not long after he delved into the Shadow Realm. However, he only chose to engage in Eitr research some time after this.
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : No one knows why His Majesty the Tsar chose to do such a thing.
<color=#ffd680>Tell me about Pavlina...</color>
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : Pavlina, princess of the Snegurochka. One of the primary researchers, she could use her superlative Prime Ice construction skills to create facilities with temperatures suitable for research.
<color=#36ffff>Eye of Graeae</color> : It seems that she once preserved many items obtained from Hyperborean ruins using Prime Ice techniques at His Majesty the Belyi Tsar's behest.

desc.text:
(A yellowed document that seems to have grown quite brittle due to an overly dry environment, written in a cold, stiff hand with almost no variation...)
I have no love for Larisa.
Though she may own all that I own, and possess Prime Ice artisanry equal to mine.
Though she may be my better in ceremonial and etiquette, such that even the previous princess, harshest amongst us, praised her.
Though... all amongst our kin love her, believing her to be noble, elegant, and a perfect fit with all that people imagine a Snegurochka to be.
She is a Snegovik amongst Snegovik, ever so perfect and impeccable.
But I do not like her.
...
A Snegovik's love is a sacrifice, a form of voluntary exchange.
You open your heart and take all from it, then expect the one you love to take all from his and give it to you.
But you, Larisa. The Prime Ice creation skills you have honed, your graceful actions, your gentle words...
Does that all exist for the sake of "sacrifice"? In your everyday life, the sharpening of your arts, in the many moments you spent caring for the flowers... Where were you? Where could you be found in them?
I asked her about this once.
But she was not offended by this question. She simply looked at me with an expression I cannot name, yet one that was almost sad, and said:
"Your heart is sealed, Pavlina. The greatest misfortune that could befall one living in this world is to love no one at all."
But must I sacrifice all for the person I love? If that is the case, then I would rather not love anyone.
The gentle words and sorrowful gaze she turned upon my doubts... all of it angered me.
Indeed, I have no love for her.
...
"The one who leads the Snegovik must have a complete soul."
Such was the instruction of our ancestor, Morevna.
And there is but one way for a Snegovik to possess a complete soul, and that is to seek true love.
Larisa brought her chosen lover back to Hesperides with her, and when by his side, she reveals such vistas of joy heretofore unseen.
Does that really make her so happy?
The decision she made in choosing her lover... Did she make it as part of the path our princess must take...
...Or did it come from the heart?
Many of our kin praise the man by her side. They say he is a handsome human. That they are a fine match, he and Larisa.
But I find him ugly and rude besides. His vulgar behavior is hardly a harmonious pair with her elegance.
When they appear together, I cannot help but feel frustrated, even nauseous.
Her taste, I suppose, must be terrible.
I have never liked those with a poor sense of aesthetics.
I suppose that is why I have never liked Larisa.
...
That man! He deserves it. He deserves it! He deserved to have his flesh and blood flensed from his bones by blades forged from wind and snow alike!
How dare he have second thoughts at this most important of ceremonies! Did he not know that you had sacrificed your life for this, Larsia!?
And yet he fled in the midst of the ritual — that cowardly human filth! That rat! That thief!
You too, Larisa! You who received no reply, you who were so annoying, you who had terrible taste... You deserved this!
But Larisa, oh, Larisa...
Were you ever so furious? Ever so sad?
Behold the clouds, how they stop for you! Even the thunder has been seized by your desire to set all to rights...
If this was the real you, you as you are now, why did you not burst into fury at these ridiculous rules earlier?
Why did you not show forth your wrath at this false "love" that we must offer up?
Why were you not... enraged at me when I doubted you?
Why did your body become so fragile when I raced toward you through the blizzard?
Why were the joy and laughter that once graced your face, indeed all of you, so quickly reduced to snow-foam amidst the frigid winds, like tears...
...And when they fell on my face, why were they no colder than a single drop of icy rain?
...
Later, I ascended to become the princess of the Snegovik. Strange, I say. Most strange. Should not one who leads us be this so-called complete soul?
A truly ancient Snegurochka, one held in high esteem amongst us, looked deeply into my eyes as she held the ceremony and said, "Sometimes, these things also happen."
What does she mean, "these things also happen"!?
If this throne could be inherited without finding true love... what was Larisa's sacrifice for, then!?
How long must our race be bound by these strange rules...
I must find it... I must find a way to resolve this. For the sake of my kin, trapped and bound by this absurdity they call "love."
For...
For Larisa, for whom I held no love.

(A note, written in a cold, stiff hand with almost no variation...)
"...The prisoners used as experimental material have already been handed over to Alvis. There is no doubt that the results of that experiment were 'incorrect.'"
"But is that what humans... Is that what loveless fae should seek as 'love'? Perhaps the Snegovik, incomplete in spirit as they are, truly could make use of this technology..."
"To gain the 'love' they lacked from the beginning. Just as... just as 'he' told me, dreams that are too grand have no meaning. Perhaps..."
"Perhaps 'he' was right. That power... That power should have been ours from the start, as compensation. It was never meant to belong to Aksinya's aberrant dream."
"...I will stop here before Alvis 'accidentally' comes across this again and causes more trouble."

(A note, written in an elegant hand...)
"I will be returning to the House of Hesperides for the next few days, so I'll leave the cat in your care. I can hardly trust the others with her, given how absorbed they become in their experiments."
"I am sure my colleague Koshchei shares my respect for living things and will remember to feed my Lara... The key and specially prepared cat food are on your desk."
"P.S. If I find that my cat has not been properly fed, or that she has somehow grown parts from another animal, I will find out who is responsible. — Pavlina"
"...And remember, my Lara only eats from her bowl. Please don't scatter her food on the floor. She won't eat anything off the floor."
